extracted.intended_audience: sports reporters, editors, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and producing sports stories using specialist newsworthiness criteria adapted from the seven core news values; includes sports-distinct values and implicit reporting skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — Most Critical for Sports
rubrics_metrics.description: "If your provincial team won a national title, the media wants to hear about it immediately, not two weeks later."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Live game updates; Same-day post-game analysis; Trade deadline coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that center on contests, disputes, tensions or opposing forces in sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Championship finals; Rivalries; Player vs. management; Sport-vs-sport; Tribunal disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Events or developments involving well-known figures or institutions that attract attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Star athletes; Famous coaches; Iconic teams; Olympic / World Cup level; Hall of Fame milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extremes / Superlatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories about exceptional outcomes or records that stand out from the ordinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Records broken; First-ever achievements; Statistical anomalies; Unprecedented streaks; Championship history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that have measurable effects on communities, public health, civic life, or economies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/angles: Local team success → community joy; Closure of community sports facilities; Health implications (concussions); Civic pride; Economic impact (stadium deals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal, emotional, or character-driven elements that make sports stories resonate beyond results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Personal struggles overcome; Rivalries with backstory; Underdog comebacks; Behind-the-scenes dynamics; Athlete activism / personal causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic or community closeness that increases relevance for a given audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Local teams covered most; Regional rivalries; Hometown angles for nationally-known athletes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Unusual
rubrics_metrics.description: Odd, unexpected, or bizarre occurrences that make a sports event stand out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Bizarre plays; Weird records; Strange weather affecting games; Animal interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical thresholds reached by players or teams that mark notable achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '1000 goals', '100 wins' — use as a clear, quantifiable hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streak / consecutive games
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable continued sequences of results or appearances that attract attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat long streaks or broken streaks as newsworthy because they indicate sustained performance or its end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comeback narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories framed around recovery or return to form after adversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Underdog comebacks; athlete recoveries — valuable for narrative-driven features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greatness debates
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussions comparing players or teams for all-time status (GOAT conversations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical context and milestones to fuel or adjudicate debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calendar events
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduled major sporting events that draw predictable attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Super Bowl, Olympics — timing around these events increases newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-field news of athletes
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-competition developments in athletes' lives that affect public perception or careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: legal issues, personal life developments — can shift or deepen coverage beyond performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Player movement and roster changes that alter team composition or competitive balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Trades, drafts — immediate coverage and analysis expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring, firing, or movement of coaching staff with implications for team direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as organizational news with analysis of strategy and culture impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports betting / fantasy implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Developments that affect wagering markets or fantasy-sports participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: injuries, lineup changes, or suspensions that change betting lines or fantasy value — angle stories to these audiences when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative power
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to craft and lead a story with compelling arcs, characters, and stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit examples: personal struggles, rivalries — use narrative framing to increase reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behind-the-scenes access
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive or insider access that yields information, context, or visuals unavailable elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for features, locker-room insights, training/process stories; improves uniqueness and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporter understanding of rules, tactics, and context needed to explain and analyze action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary for accurate play-by-play, analysis pieces, and informed interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stat literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to interpret, contextualize, and communicate statistics meaningfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to support claims (e.g., records, anomalies) and to fuel greatness debates or analytical pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely production
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to produce and publish content quickly enough to meet sports audiences' expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tied to 'Timeliness' news value — live updates, same-day analysis, and rapid reaction pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of photos, video, audio, and interactive elements to enhance storytelling and immediacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate for live coverage, highlight reels, interactive stats, and richer feature presentation.
